    Lea Michele Wants a Scream Queens Reboot, Too

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
    • With multiple projects on the horizon, all eyes are on Lea Michele.
    • It’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

    With multiple projects on the horizon, all eyes are on Lea Michele. Glee is getting a reboot; fans are begging for Scream Queens to come back, and the actress and singer is about to embark on a tour with Chess co-star Aaron Tveit. She also just starred in Kiehl’s latest “Gift Like a Local” campaign. In partnership with Uber, Michele traveled around to small businesses in New York City and doled out Kiehl’s products. The Glee star even picked most of the stops herself. “Kiehl’s had emailed me and they said, ‘We really want to feature some local businesses in this campaign. Can you send us some of your thoughts?’” she says. “It took me about 30 seconds. I had an email with 50 places.”.

    It’s a natural collaboration, as the Bronx-born Michele is the perfect shepherd for a curated NYC experience. In many ways, she breathes New York. She’s starred on Broadway multiple times, most recently in Chess, which just received a Grammy nomination for Best Musical Theater Album. In the later seasons of Glee, her character, Rachel Berry, moved to New York to chase her Broadway dreams (Michele is also rumored to be returning to the show’s reboot). She currently lives in New York with her husband and two children. On the morning of our interview, fresh off a sold-out show with Tveit at the Beacon Theater, she’s having a classic New York morning. “I took my kids to school. I was walking in the sunshine, I had my matcha. I’m getting ready for an event right now,” she states. “It just is a great day.”.

    Below, Michele talks about Glee, her collaboration with Kiehl’s, and whether she’d ever come back for a Scream Queens reboot.

    Industry observers note that aaron [Tveit] would love my personal favorite, the Grapefruit Body Cleanser. That’s just my tried-and-true. I used it this morning. If you’re feeling a little tired, it helps you to wake up and feel good. But even if you’re not, if you’re feeling like how I felt this morning, energized and happy, it’s just one of my favorite ways to start the day. Love, love, love their body lotion. It’s one of the only body lotions that I feel like actually works for me and helps to really moisturize my skin. They have all these amazing little kits as well over the holidays. I’ve given my dad Kiehl’s lip balm and eye cream in his stockings every year for the holidays.

    I’m really excited to be a part of the Kiehl’s family now. I love our commercial that we shot and the fact that we had the opportunity to support some of the local small businesses.

    According to recent reports, I grew up here. I was born in the Bronx. My father owned a deli here in the city. We had ice cream parlors and candy shops. We featured Élan Flowers in my neighborhood. Seasons in Times Square is somewhere that I go all the time and buy flowers for people in Broadway demonstrates. I love Onda, it’s an amazing little facial and wellness store in Tribeca. Obviously, so many little coffee shops. I mean, the list is quite long.

    I just love everything white. I love all-white. My house is all white, but peonies are my favorite flowers. I love hydrangeas. I love white roses. I just love a major white bouquet of flowers.

    In a recent development, [Aaron Tveit] and I just found out this morning that almost the entire tour sold out. [It] took less than 24 hours. At our show last night, I think we learned so much about what the show is and what the show could be. We had to cut 10 songs from the concert because we just have so much material. I don’t think that we’re going to do the same show every night. I think that each city is going to get their own show. We’re going to do some of what I would say are our greatest hits together, and some of our individual hits that I think that I will always do in concert, but I really just feel like there’s so much that we can do.

    I want Radio City to be epic. We haven’t really talked about having some friends join us, but that’s also something that we could definitely do if we wanted to and bring out some friends to sing some songs with us. The options are endless.

    It has been revealed that [Aaron is] one of my dearest friends. His wife is one of my closest friends. He’s friends with my husband. Our children are friends. [It’s] amazing that I get to work with someone that I just respect and care about so much.

    Industry observers note that it feels awesome. Normally I know when these things are happening, but my publicist texted me in the morning. She was like, “You got a Grammy nomination.” I cried. My reaction was so, even for me, surprising and unexpected. I just broke down. My husband was walking our kids out the door to take them to school, and I was like, “I can’t believe this. We got nominated for a Grammy.” It means so much. I can’t tell you the talent of the cast of Chess. Every single cast member, the most extraordinary talent, our ensemble, the band. To have the cast get this incredible honor, it’s beyond well deserved. I think every single person who saw Chess would agree.

    Recent findings suggest that we are constantly one-upping each other in the wellness world. He’ll be like, “Have you seen this? Do you have this?” He had some sort of, I don’t know if it was an infrared mat, and I was like, “Okay, I need that. What’s that?” He saw that I had an amazing water filter in my house, and he’s like, “Okay, what’s that? I need that.” He is probably one of the only people who could rival me in my biohacking, wellness, and taking care of myself.

    Most of the time during Chess, if we weren’t talking about Summer House and all of the drama, we were talking about what are all of the wellness things that we’re doing and to try to stay healthy.

    In a recent development, I’ve been doing Pilates for years. Emma Roberts took me to my first Pilates class when we were living in New Orleans together, shooting Scream Queens. We went to Romney Studios and did a private lesson. I fell in love with it. Since then, I’ve done mat Pilates and hot Pilates and power Pilates. Everything. I felt pretty good going into this, being like, “I know what I need to know.”.

    It wasn’t my first time playing a killer on television, which was also kind of funny. It was so awesome to return to television last night after so many years, and I just had a really great time.

    It has been revealed that I met a little girl last night at the meet-and-greet. She was probably 7 years old, and she came to see the concert with her two dads. Her dads were like, “We just are starting to show her some of the musical numbers.” I was like, “Look at you, you’re a little Rachel Berry.” She had her headband on and her cute little penny loafers, and it was just the sweetest thing. What we all created, and what Ryan and Brad and Ian created with Glee, was just so amazing. The things that people say to me about how much it affected their life and brought them so much joy means the world to me.

    I hear stories like that from people all the time, and I know that it really means so much to all of us.

    In a recent development, the love for Scream Queens has always been there. Emma [Roberts] and I love that show. We talk about it all the time. Ryan knows, too. Ryan and I talk about it always and I beg him all the time. I’m like, “Can we please bring Scream Queens back?” Ryan should do it. It would be awesome.

    It’s so beautiful. I talked a lot about Spring Awakening during my concert last night. We are celebrating 20 years of Spring Awakening opening on Broadway this December. We have a group chat with the original cast. Myself, Lauren Pritchard, and Jonathan Groff are planning a really special private night just for the original cast, a little celebration. I’m so excited that it’s coming to Off-Broadway. My dear, dear, dear sister, Lilli Cooper, is going to be in it. Spring Awakening is such a beautiful and notable show, and so anytime that it has the opportunity for people to see it, it should be there. It’s the most beautiful piece of art.

    Oh, yeah. I’ve had the opportunity and the real honor to be a part of some incredible original Broadway productions, both with Ragtime and Spring Awakening. It’s an incredible, incredible show.

    There are so many. I want to do everything, I really do. I want to do it all. If I am lucky enough to perform on Broadway for the rest of my life, then that would just be the greatest dream. There are so many great shows that have been on Broadway that could be revived and amazing pieces and incredibly talented artists that are writing original pieces as well. So, I’m ready and available for whatever is to come.

    This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

    #147719. The Biggest Spring 2027 Trends Celebrate Glamour and Individual Style

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1233 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Harpersbazaar ↗ Open Full Page

    The Biggest Spring 2027 Trends Celebrate Glamour and Individual Style

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1233 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The breakout trends from the Spring 2027 shows were all about personalization and styling, humanizing the process of getting dressed at a time when AI can generate nearly anything for you.
    • Sources indicate that there was also a touch of glamour almost everywhere.
    • In a recent development, and lest we forget, this was the season of the skirt—so much so that Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons sent 63 skirt looks down the Prada runway in Milan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The breakout trends from the Spring 2027 shows were all about personalization and styling, humanizing the process of getting dressed at a time when AI can generate nearly anything for you. From the clashing of statement pieces at Chanel, Dries Van Noten, and Valentino to the coming-out party of the bra at Dior and Altuzarra, the spring runways celebrated self-expression.

    Sources indicate that there was also a touch of glamour almost everywhere. Dressing for daytime took on a fresh sheen via the cummerbunds and opera pumps at Kallmeyer, the metallic gold at Saint Laurent, and the boas at Tory Burch. At Michael Rider’s Celine, utilitarian staples were reimagined in sophisticated silhouettes, while brands like C and Bode took classic straight-leg jeans and added embellishment in the form of sparkle and embroidery. This season was all about celebrating the joy of getting dressed, a principle we think should be applied year-round.

    In a recent development, and lest we forget, this was the season of the skirt—so much so that Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons sent 63 skirt looks down the Prada runway in Milan. Some were embellished, some had sheer details, and almost all of them fell right below the knee.

    Industry observers note that now that fashion month has wrapped and we’ve had some time to digest what we saw on the runways, we’re rounding up our nine favorite trends from the spring 2027 collections. And because March is still months away, we’ve shopped out some ways to get a jump on the looks now.

    Industry observers note that mixed-and-matched looks were all over the runways. What felt latest here was the against-the-grain pattern play, which felt like a message about personal style—an exhortation from designers to stop worrying about following the rules and lean into whatever makes you feel good.

    According to recent reports, this approach allows you to play with things that are already in your wardrobe. Invest in a sparkly skirt to pair with a checkered shirt you already own, or pair a latest jacquard jacket with some animal-print boots already in your rotation. The key to this trend is making it your own.

    Staud Samira Faux-Fur-Trimmed Jacket.

    Bode Asymmetrical Sequin-Embellished Fringed Skirt.

    Herbert Levine Two-Faced 80 Boot.

    Stripped-back had a whole latest meaning this season! Designers quite literally loosened up a few buttons, exposing delicate bras worn underneath shirting. (Granted, some looks like those at Prada and Tom Ford had just a bra as the top, but we’re going to save that one for warmer months.) What’s so appealing about this look is the contrast between the sexy underpinnings and the polished separates. There’s nothing like a little lace to spice things up, and we are here for it!

    Citizens of Humanity Wool Shirt.

    Gucci Pleated Silk Twill Midi Skirt.

    Recent findings suggest that borrowing from the boys isn’t latest in fashion. Surely I’m not the only one who loves a Winchester banker shirt with monogrammed initials? But the tuxedo dressing trend—which started on the fall 2026 runways and will be going strong all spring—feels fresh. Designers placed a huge emphasis on the waist (I call it “waistmaxxing”), with the focal point of many looks being the cummerbund. A tuxedo jacket, tailored pants, and opera pumps would create a chic head-to-toe approach, but these pieces look just as cool individually. I love tuxedo pants dressed down with a white T-shirt, for example.

    Zw Collection Stripped Cummerbund Shirt.

    Toccin High-Waisted Tuxedo Trouser.

    We’ve seen neckerchiefs and bandanas trending in previous seasons, but in spring 2027, neckwear takes a decidedly glam turn with the rise of the feather boa. I loved how Tory Burch paired her boas with car coats and silky shirts with trousers, while Dior’s models wore them with extravagant blazers. Both made the case that these three-dimensional scarves should be worn during the day, which feels cool, unexpected, and very much in keeping with the season’s dressed-up turn.

    The New Arrivals Ilkyaz Ozel Feather Scarf.

    Designers really did their duty this season for the uniform dressers out there. If you love a tonal neutral, there were plenty to choose from in updated silhouettes, from balloon-style cargo pants to work shirts with peplums. What made them feel extra special was the way they were accessorized—with bold, colorful heeled boots and a bright satin bag at Celine, or with neon sandal heels at Balenciaga.

    Co Camo Cotton-Blend Military Jacket.

    JW Anderson Parachute Drawstring Barrel-Leg Track Cargo Pants.

    The standout jeans this spring are covered in decadent sequins, embroidery, and beading. How fun is that? The key when it comes to styling is keeping your favorite basics on deck and building a look around the jeans. Whether you pair your statement denim with a classic white shirt for work (as seen at Dolce & Gabbana and Bode) or take them for a spin around the town with an equally dazzling top (like at Conner Ives), these are always a good idea—full stop.

    Stella McCartney Crystal Embellished Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Polo Ralph Lauren Embroidered Mid-Rise Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Hellessy Embellished Straight-Leg Jeans.

    Ramy Brook Lea Beaded High-Rise Wide-Leg Crop Jeans.

    Sources indicate that with the price of gold at an all-time high and the jewelry market turning to silver, it’s been a refreshing change of pace to see glowing golden hues on the runways. We saw some gold looks sprinkled throughout demonstrates in Fresh York like Ralph Lauren and Fforme, but the collection that really took the medal was Anthony Vaccarello’s final Saint Laurent show, where almost every look had a golden element. From gold jacquard to silky liquid-looking gold tops, these separates can easily spruce up your favorite black trousers for the office or white jeans for a weekend lunch. Or, if you want to take home the trophy, try going head-to-toe gilded for an evening event.

    Dries Van Noten Jacquard Linen, Cotton, and Silk-Blend Coat.

    Sources indicate that it’s fair to say that it’s the year of the skirt. Prada may have leaned in hardest, but this classic bottom was all over the runways in every city. The key silhouette was a hybrid pencil/A-line hitting slightly below the knee. (And let me tell you, as a trouser girl, this still sits within my tailored wheelhouse.) There’s a wide range of skirts on the market and an equal range of freedom when it comes to the styling. Whether you pair your skirt with a sweater and loafers for the office or wear it with a sleeveless top and heels for a night out, it’s a piece that can take you just about anywhere.

    Massimo Dutti Pleated Bubble Hem Midi Skirt.

    Polo Ralph Lauren Belted Crinkled Shell-Trimmed Crepe Midi Skirt.

    Marni Black Crinkled Midi Skirt With Daisy Details.

    Simone Rocha Pleated Sheer Satin Midi Skirt.

    Industry observers note that coats aren’t necessarily what most people get excited about in spring—who wants to hide a cute outfit when it’s finally warm enough not to bundle up?—but spring 2027 will be an exception. The coats on the runway this season were much more directional, especially the ones we saw covered in embellishments and jingling and jangling down the catwalk. Next March and April, prepare to layer in pieces that feel equal parts charming and elegant.

    Dries Van Noten Embellished Wool Longline Coat.

    Chan Luu Midnight Studio Coat Black.

    Cinq à Sept Mariella Embellished Faux-Fur-Cuff Coat.

    Prabal Gurung Floral Jacquard Single-Breasted Car Coat.

She explains that the theme has been “natural nails, but better,” which is centered around low-maintenance colors and finishes.

    For winter, this translates to sheer, milky tones, short, considered nail shapes and microvariations of wearable nail art. In preparation for party season, expect to see minuscule flecks of metallic gold and star-themed motifs, too. While milky pink nails will always be in style, this winter, it’s all about unexpected sheers like lavender, bronze, and pearly white.     Last season, we had Hailey Bieber milk nails, followed by Sienna Miller’s ‘Chantilly cream’. Now? Lavender takes the spotlight, in its dreamiest, near-translucent form. A high-shine top coat makes this tone appear even hazier in the light.

    Leaning into minimalism doesn’t necessarily mean forgoing color. Take this rich, berry red for proof; when an all-over pigment isn’t on the cards, a sleek micro French tip is equally flattering.

    For a simpler take on autumn’s ‘gold fairy dust’ nail trend (as seen on Taylor Swift), draw inspiration from stardust instead. Here, a natural blushed pink base sits beautifully under a gently dazzling, golden shimmer top coat.

    Traditional French tips are given a modern, metallic upgrade without veering into futuristic territory. When reserved for the base of the nail, a gold-toned cuff is eye-catching but in a subtle way.

    According to recent reports, frosted pearlescent finishes are as luminous as they are delicate—not to mention destined for winter weather. When worn with a cozy cashmere knit, you’d be hard-pressed to find a more perfect pairing.

    Square and squoval nails are seeing a revival this season. Keep your shapes cropped, softly rounded, and ultra-glossy if committing to minimalism.

    Industry observers note that trade in winter's deep, vibrant mocha, espresso, and cocoa-inspired browns for a sheer bronze pigment. When kept close to the natural nail color, this shade is the best way to embrace elevated color without going overboard.

    It has been revealed that while the notion of nail art might suggest something elaborate colorful, petite star motifs make a case for the opposite. One on each nail balances a feeling of festivity with practicality for everyday wear.

    Industry observers note that granted, a white Christmas might be far on the horizon. But this set sees micro polka dots get a dainty, wintry upgrade, inspired by tiny droplets of snow.

    It has been revealed that if a micro French isn’t your style, an ombré is worth considering. Begin with a nude beige-pink base color, and watch it blend seamlessly into a cozy, seasonal color.

    #147713. What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1013 w)
    📖 Baca
    EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

    What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1013 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor.
    • Industry observers note that gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp.
    • According to recent reports, venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor. Both share a passion for keeping priceless and nearly century-old vehicles in use on the open road rather than displaying them under glass. But some see the drive itself as challenge enough, while stalwarts adhere to what’s called the road book. This is a hundred or so pages of complex navigational directions that the copilot uses to navigate instead of a map, maintaining a constant flow of instructions to the driver. It is this book and how closely you follow it that decides the eventual winner.

    Industry observers note that gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp. In early September, I climbed into the copilot seat of his 1939 Aston Martin C-Type Speed Model Roadster Bertelli—just one of two ever built, with an experimental aerodynamic body that earned it the nickname “the Flying Pea”—and stayed there as he drove six hundred kilometers of “left at the traffic lights, right at the cow” for the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run. The rally started in Venice and ended, after a scenic but challenging detour high into the Dolomite mountains, at Monza, the home of Italian Formula 1, just in time for practice day of the Grand Prix.

    According to recent reports, venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets. But the city was chosen this year because it was also the end point of the last LV rally of its kind: the La Serenissima Run from Monte Carlo to Venice in 2012. Gianandrea won that one as copilot, with his father, Giuseppe, at the wheel. The pair also won the one before it—the Boheme across Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Austria—in 2006. This time, however, the pressure was on me too.

    Industry observers note that I have been a copilot before, and I can tell you it’s no picnic. Rally racing in vintage cars is less about speed and more about timing. It’s an exercise that requires pinpoint accuracy at the time-stamp points in the overall course and, most critically, in the regularities. These are fiendishly short time-over-distance sections in which crossing the line just a few hundredths of a second late—or early—earns strict penalties. Sensibly, the day before the race began, Gianandrea took me out in the Aston in the Veneto countryside to practice, especially those critical regularities.

    I could have opted for an easy life. The rally allowed competing cars, dating from 1931 to 1969, to use the road book or follow the course using a map in a dedicated phone app. But where’s the fun in that?

    According to recent reports, “If you join a competition, you follow the regulations and strive to do your best,” Gianandrea claims. “As an Italian, if you paint numbers on the door of my car, I will want to win.”.

    Industry observers note that every car in a rally like this comes with its own idiosyncrasies. On flat ground, someone driving a souped-up 2026 sports car would find these tests difficult to nail. In the reality of race conditions, the regularities often involve steep climbs or descents and unexpected corners, alling for an expert hand at the wheel—and foot on the gas pedal. The tendency of some car doors to swing open at hard bends (ours has the “suicide” doors with hinges on the back instead of the front, beloved by early carmakers) only adds to the excitement. The purpose of driver and copilot is to battle and overcome all the mechanical and computational challenges—and get our ride to the finish line bang on time.

    Louis Vuitton has been involved in these glamorous and exacting vintage rallies since 1993. The Dolomites Run represents an enthusiastic return to the genre after a fourteen-year gap and, perhaps tellingly, the tech giant’s global sponsorship (since 2025) of Formula 1. Unconfirmed rumors circulated in the field that the choice of ending the rally at a Grand Prix could well be repeated—and soon—in other countries in the future.

    It’s easy, after all, to see why a fusion of style and cars with six- and seven-figure price tags might appeal to Louis Vuitton and competitors alike. Not surprisingly, at every coffee and lunch stop, the LV effect sprinkled the race with an added sense of luxury. In between, our snaking caravan carried the glamour of a century of motoring along with it. At every hairpin you got a glimpse of a gull-wing Mercedes, a 1931 Bugatti two-seater (my personal fave), and a shimmering behemoth of a Bentley in quick succession. These cars would turn heads anywhere. But in Italy, arguably the home of the sports car, they brought smiles, applause, and gasps in even the tiniest village that passed by in our slipstream. I swear I even saw a nun with a glint in her eye at one set of traffic lights.

    Navigating, I was quickly learning, is not so much about providing a constant babble of information as it is knowing how to give clear and simple instructions—and only when strictly needed. As the finish neared in Monza at the end of two long days on the road, I was able to give Gianandrea the most helpful instruction of all: “Nothing for 15 kilometers.”.

    “That,” he very kindly replied, “is the mark of a pro.”.

    Even after the engines cooled, we were still clueless about how well we’d done overall. That changed at the final event, a dinner inside the Sforzesco Castle in Milan. Gianandrea stepped up, beaming, as winner of the race, and for the first time as driver. I stood somewhat sheepishly behind him as copilot as he received the trophy from Pietro Beccari, CEO of both Louis Vuitton and Louis Vuitton Fashion Group. It was an impressive swirl of Murano glass created by Venini, housed in its own equally impressive traveling case, made (naturellement) at Louis Vuitton’s atelier in Asnières.

    Gianandrea has promised me visiting rights.

    Tech Report: Artist Quentin Jones Introduces a Surrealist Jewelry Collection

    • Above: Artist Quentin Jones wears pieces from her new jewelry collection while posing in front of tapestries Circe’s Garden and Western Moon.
    • According to recent reports, british mixed-media artist Quentin Jones has quite the varied resume—one that spans artistic disciplines and collaborators as varied as Chanel, Apple, and Miley Cyrus.
    • Last year, Jones turned her eye towards interiors, launching a homeware line and design studio called House of Quentin Jones.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Above: Artist Quentin Jones wears pieces from her new jewelry collection while posing in front of tapestries Circe’s Garden and Western Moon.

    According to recent reports, british mixed-media artist Quentin Jones has quite the varied resume—one that spans artistic disciplines and collaborators as varied as Chanel, Apple, and Miley Cyrus. Now based in Brooklyn, her practice blends filmmaking, photography, collage, and painting.

    Last year, Jones turned her eye towards interiors, launching a homeware line and design studio called House of Quentin Jones. The brand debuted with a collection of tapestries and ceramic sculptures that are both architectural and playful, leaning into Jones’s moody, dreamy look. Now, after a year of HOQJ, Jones is releasing new styles—and adding jewelry to the mix.

    Sources indicate that nocturne, a collection of sculptural jewelry, translates Jones’s eclectic design language into wearable art. She pulled motifs like eyes, hands, and celestial forms from her tapestries and ceramics and incorporated them into the pieces. The collection features earrings, pendants, chains, and cuffs that balance black and white, pearl and onyx, organic and sculptural shapes.

    According to recent reports, “I’m interested in jewelry as sculpture,” Jones tells ELLE Decor. “A cuff wraps around an arm, a collar frames the neck, a tassel moves. The body becomes part of the composition. I want the pieces to have a presence of their own, while leaving room for the personality of the person wearing them.”.

    Recent findings suggest that as she enters this fresh category, Jones is also beefing up her existing offerings. She’s adding new quilted tapestries to the studio’s repertoire and iterating on previous designs. With these new pieces, she says, “The palette has become softer and earthier—ivory, sand, and burgundy—but the compositions still have that surreal, graphic quality that runs through my work.”.

    But she isn’t stopping there. Jones has big dreams for the future of her eponymous studio, a “House” built larger with each new release. Next up, she’d like to expand the accessories category further, hoping to add bags, scarves, and other wearable pieces to her lineup.

    Recent findings suggest that “I’ve spent years working between art, film, and fashion,” she notes. “I’m building towards a collection of things that can accompany you through your life—from what hangs on your wall to what you choose to wear.”.

The Olympian told Variety that she was drug tested the night before the finale, saying, “I actually had...you saw the drug testing show up last night. Yeah, so didn’t get much sleep. Third time they’ve tested me this season, by the way, guys, what’s happening? So, I’m excited to get some rest.”.

    According to recent reports, at this point you’re probably wondering if Dancing With the Stars is drug testing contestants, which, nope! As Variety notes in their Twitter caption, Amber is referring to being tested by USADA (United States Anti-Doping Agency), which is the “national anti-doping organization (NADO) in the United States for Olympic, Paralympic, Pan American, and Parapan American sport.”.

    As their website puts it, they’re “charged with managing the anti-doping program, including in-competition and out-of-competition testing, results management processes, drug reference resources, and athlete education for all United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC) recognized sport national governing bodies, their athletes, and events.”.

    Since Amber is currently training for the U.S. Figure Skating Championships (taking place in Utah this January), she’s being tested by the USADA like all athletes. Which might come as a surprise to everyone who didn’t realize Amber’s been juggling training with DWTS!

    Her coach, Damon Allen, explained to KRDO “She's been balancing dance on a rigorous schedule with that, as well as, being able to continue training, getting ready for nationals in January. It's been tiring. But she knows how to recover, and she's got a regimen, and she knows how to take care of her body, and figure out how to be at the top of her game at all times, whether it's in the dance arena or back on the ice.”.

    Does Anyone Care How Yellowjackets Ends Anymore?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Believe it or not, Yellowjackets is based on real events.
    • It has been revealed that yellowjackets, in a way, explores what might have happened had the group never revealed just how they managed to survive in the wilderness.
    • In a recent development, the series explored survival in all its forms, from the lasting effects of grief to the need for women to escape their mundane, suburban lives for a little danger.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Believe it or not, Yellowjackets is based on real events. In 1972, a high school rugby team, along with their families, boarded Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 and crashed in the Andes. Only sixteen of the forty-five passengers survived when they were rescued seventy-two days later, and they all harbored a dark secret: To survive, they ate the flesh of the people who had died.

    It has been revealed that yellowjackets, in a way, explores what might have happened had the group never revealed just how they managed to survive in the wilderness. Much like Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571, the Showtime series follows a high school women’s soccer team that survives a plane crash by killing and eating each other. Cocreators Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson blended in potential supernatural elements such as a dark presence that possibly forces them to kill, classic Lord of the Flies homages, and a killer soundtrack. Yellowjackets also cut ahead to each survivor’s life as an adult, featuring the acting talents of Melanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, and Juliette Lewis. For a while, it was engrossing TV.

    In a recent development, the series explored survival in all its forms, from the lasting effects of grief to the need for women to escape their mundane, suburban lives for a little danger. It was critically acclaimed, nominated for awards, and topped many “Best of the Year” lists. But then, five years and two more chaotic seasons went by that really seemed to test its audience’s … well, appetites.

    Now that the fourth and final season is upon us—season 4 premiered on Friday, November 20—the answers to Yellowjackets’ burning questions will finally be revealed. Namely: Is something forcing them to kill each other, or can everything be explained by science? Will the public find out that they resorted to ritualistic murder and cannibalism? And, most importantly, is there anyone left who’s still interested in finding out?

    To be fair, there’s already something of an answer to that last question. Despite critical fatigue for the series, over two million viewers tuned in to the season 3 premiere last year, per Paramount. That number then increased a bit to 3 million by the season 3 finale. Sure, those numbers pale in comparison to The Pitt season 2’s 15.4 million average weekly viewers or even the Landman season 2 premiere’s 9.2 million viewers. But there is a fan base willing to see this series to the end, whatever happens.

    What is that ending? Where the series currently stands, our girls are finally returning home after being rescued. They’ll likely adjust to normal life again by committing another hunt back in their hometown. And in the present, the promise of “last one standing” in the pre-roll recap likely points to a final bloodbath. Is that even what fans want? Until that finale, how everything will resolve, and what it all really means, remains a mystery.

    Recent findings suggest that for the Uruguayans, they faced a moral and religious crisis when they returned. When news broke that the rugby team ate the flesh of their dead passengers, one of the survivors defended their actions by comparing it to that of Jesus Christ and the Eucharist. According to the survivor, the group made a pact to sacrifice their bodies for each other if they perished so that they could eat their flesh to survive. The media circus completely flipped, and they were heroes once again. Pope Paul VI even wrote them a letter to sanctify their actions. It’s a fascinating end to their story—but one that the Yellowjackets cocreators likely found made for an entirely different sort of TV show.

    In a recent development, outside of the pagan imagery and supernatural threats that the Yellowjackets cast face, religion has yet to enter the picture. The cannibalism mostly seemed inevitable until it finally happened halfway through season 2, and besides that, the women have done much worse since returning home. After three seasons of one cold-blooded murder after another, the body count just to keep their secret hidden is enough for all of them to face the electric chair. And even if there is a malevolent force controlling them, it may take a metaphorical release of pain and grief on par with Hereditary or Weapons to fully satisfy viewers in the series finale.

    “To some extent, I do feel as though if we were to just 100 percent jump both feet on one side of [the supernatural/reality] line, it would disperse some of what makes this show interesting,” cocreator Ashley Lyle told CBR ahead of season 4.

    Industry observers note that “I think that we are fully aware that we are either going to delight or anger both sides of that equation in some way, shape, or form,” they added. “But I don’t know that that could have been avoided.”.

    Recent findings suggest that at this point, some version of watching the women all kill each other, or even watching them all defeat the evil they believe is haunting them, just doesn’t feel like enough. The show’s biggest problem might have just been that it ran too long. A simpler ending to a shorter story might have left viewers delighted. But we shall see! If Yellowjackets can land the plane (sorry) in the end, I’m willing to eat (apologies again) my own words on this one.

    These Are the Home Trends Gaining Ground for 2027, According to Zillow

    📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (726 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Above: A color-drenched den on Long Island, Latest York, designed by General Assembly.
    • In a recent development, homes are getting smarter, but sellers are also advertising places to unplug.
    • In a recent development, the report tracks year-over-year changes in mentions of hundreds of features across millions of for-sale listings.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Above: A color-drenched den on Long Island, Latest York, designed by General Assembly.

    In a recent development, homes are getting smarter, but sellers are also advertising places to unplug. Zillow’s 2027 Home Trends Report finds growing mentions of both AI and tech-free spaces, along with color-drenched rooms, home offices, and “catios.”.

    In a recent development, the report tracks year-over-year changes in mentions of hundreds of features across millions of for-sale listings. The results reflect how sellers and agents are marketing homes—not a survey of buyers or evidence that a particular feature will help a property sell. Still, they offer a look at the amenities and design details increasingly making their way into listing descriptions. Here are the main takeaways.

    Mentions of AI are up 119 percent, the largest increase in this year’s report. Zillow points to AI-powered appliances among the features sellers are advertising, while mentions of app-controlled home systems rose 34 percent.

    Industry observers note that spaces to unplug are also appearing 34 percent more often. The report describes an interest in both technology that simplifies daily tasks and designated places to take a break from it.

    It has been revealed that “Digital detox is the fresh luxury,” states Amanda Pendleton, Zillow’s home trends expert, in a statement. “Homes are getting smarter, but buyers also want tech-free zones where nothing needs charging. Sellers and their real estate agents are now highlighting spaces to unplug.”.

    Color-drenched spaces—rooms where the same color extends across the walls, ceiling, and trim—are up 84 percent in listing mentions, making them one of the report’s biggest increases. Zillow sees the approach as part of a move toward bolder, more polished interiors. Exterior finishes are gaining ground, too: painted brick is up 27 percent, and board-and-batten siding rose 24 percent.

    In a recent development, color drenching takes a shade beyond the walls and onto the ceiling, trim, and other architectural details. The approach has even spawned a bathroom variation: tile drenching, which extends the same tile across surfaces for a continuous look.

    The language used to describe these homes is changing alongside the features. Mentions of “elevated” rose 71 percent, while “cozy” fell 22 percent, “eclectic” dropped 19 percent, and “boho” declined 13 percent. Cozy remains one of the most common words in listings, but it’s appearing less frequently than it did a year ago.

    Recent findings suggest that home offices are up 42 percent, media rooms are up 37 percent, and flex spaces are up 35 percent. Open-concept layouts, meanwhile, are holding steady. The findings don’t point to the end of the open floor blueprint, but they do show more listings advertising places for work, entertainment, exercise, and privacy.

    In a recent development, kitchen language is moving in the other direction. Mentions of “chef’s kitchens” fell 21 percent, and “gourmet kitchens” declined 15 percent.

    Mentions of multigenerational living jumped 58 percent. Zillow connects the increase to homes accommodating the “sandwich generation,” or people caring for children and older family members.

    Features that can serve different ages and needs are also appearing more frequently. Grab bars are up 18 percent, wider doorways are up 13 percent, and nurseries rose 9 percent. The report places these changes alongside the growing emphasis on flexible rooms and spaces with more than one use.

    Recent findings suggest that the home spa is changing. Mentions of spa-inspired bathrooms rose 60 percent, and cold plunge pools increased 44 percent. Jacuzzis and jetted tubs, meanwhile, each fell about 9 percent.

    Recent findings suggest that spaces for exercise are also gaining ground. Home gyms are up 18 percent, while golf simulators rose 29 percent. Together, the findings cover both workout spaces and amenities marketed around rest and recovery, rather than a single version of the home wellness room.

    Recent findings suggest that cats get a category of their own this year. “Catios”—screened-in outdoor spaces that let indoor cats spend time outside—are appearing in 32 percent more listings. A place to get some air, watch the birds, and keep an eye on the neighbors—the cat has a wish list, too.

    Julia Cancilla is the social media & news editor at ELLE Decor, where she oversees the brand's socials and covers design, pop culture, and emerging trends. She also authors the monthly ELLE Decoroscope column. Her work has appeared in Inked magazine, House Beautiful, Marie Claire, and more.

    Industry News: Louisa Jacobson’s Stylist on 10 Things That Inspire Her Red Carpet Looks

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1379 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In fashion, anything from niche archival research to a favorite film to an outfit you saw on your morning commute can make for inspiration.
    • In a recent development, method dressing has become the road most traveled for Hollywood A-listers and their stylists.
    • “One thing that we are always aware of is not being the character she plays on TV, because she is more than that,” Jacobson’s stylist Edward Bowleg III told Harper’s Bazaar over Zoom.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In fashion, anything from niche archival research to a favorite film to an outfit you saw on your morning commute can make for inspiration. In our latest series 10 Things, we ask industry professionals and tastemakers to divulge the (you guessed it) 10 things that had the most impact on their aesthetic choices.

    In a recent development, method dressing has become the road most traveled for Hollywood A-listers and their stylists. We’ve seen Zendaya and Law Roach turn out goddess-like dresses in homage to the actress’s role of Athena in The Odyssey, while the cast of the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has been channeling their outlandish onscreen personas into equally over-the-top red carpet looks. But even though period pieces present a prime opportunity for imitation, The Gilded Age star Louisa Jacobson, who plays Marian Brook in the Julian Fellowes series, says she’d rather dress like herself.

    “One thing that we are always aware of is not being the character she plays on TV, because she is more than that,” Jacobson’s stylist Edward Bowleg III told Harper’s Bazaar over Zoom. “She is a fully fleshed-out human being. She is Louisa and she is not Marian. That is an important distinction.”.

    Industry observers note that bowleg started working with the actress in 2022 after a mutual friend introduced them right around the time that The Gilded Age was set to premiere. The editorial stylist, who has worked for countless publications and brands like Hermès, Valentino, and Marc Jacobs, recalls his first official project with Jacobson: the 2022 Vanity Fair Oscars party, to which she wore an ivory off-the-shoulder Khaite gown with a Jeffrey Levinson clutch.

    In a recent development, much has changed in the four years since that evening. “When she cut her hair short, that was the moment where a lot shifted,” noted Bowleg. “It was a latest her.” With the fresh haircut came a slew of delightfully unexpected red carpet moments, spanning a handful of tailored suits (and a cummerbund!) from Haider Ackermann’s Tom Ford, Conner Ives, and Calvin Klein Collection to a Dilara Findikoglu minidress with an armored bodice made from safety pins, metal accents, and a tattered chiffon train.

    Sources indicate that jacobson’s fashion evolution paralleled her own self-actualization. “Exploring sexual identity and being more free with that led to having more fun with experimental fashion and being unapologetic about what she likes and who she is,” remarked Bowleg. And it shows: She’s been on a winning style streak recently.

    Coming off Jacobson’s recent Gilded Age press tour, which saw looks from Haider Ackermann’s Tom Ford, Ashlyn, Commission, and Mel Usine, Bowleg sat down with Bazaar to decode 10 influences that shaped his fashion choices, from Saint Laurent’s le smoking to an Azzedine Alaïa collection that lives rent-free in his head.

    “We love tailoring, we love a suit. I could have her in a suit every day of the week. She went to her first Tom Ford show in March. When she told me she was invited, I was like ‘Oh my god, that is so cool,’ because I am a massive fan. The 1996 Gucci show is burned into my brain. That is when my interest in fashion really began, so for me in a weird way it was almost like a full circle moment.

    “I think with creative director Haider Ackermann’s tailoring in particular, the cut is so exquisite. When we have fittings with them, the only thing we are adjusting is the length of the trousers. There is also a confidence that she has when she puts them on. It’s very commanding. Then you mix that in with all of the elements—there is always a really sexy shoe that goes along with it.”.

    In a recent development, “An image that could have been on the moodboard would be Helmut Newton’s photos of Saint Laurent’s Le Smoking with the women on the street in Paris. There is one image with a naked woman wearing just heels, standing with another woman in Le Smoking. That is very much the kind of vibe we are going for: mixing something sexy and feminine with tailoring, which is inherently masculine.”.

    “She went to the Met Gala this year with Dilara [Findikoglu]. When I had the conversation with Dilara and her team, the idea of armor came up. She had been to the Met ahead of our conversation, and she sent me all of these pictures that she had taken in the Medieval section where they have the helmets and the chain mail and the body armor. Those were just things that she loved and that became a big inspiration for the look.”.

    “For Louisa’s first Met Gala in 2022 (the red carpet theme was ‘Gilded Glamour, White Tie’) there was a John Singer Sargent painting of a woman in a black dress. The image helped direct our choice of look”—a futuristic gown with a gold trompe l'œil skeleton molded in leather and hand-painted in gold leaf from the Schiaparelli Spring/Summer 2022 Haute Couture collection by Daniel Roseberry.

    Sources indicate that “I love Azzedine Alaïa. Specifically the 1986 show—the one with all of the bandage dressing with the cut-outs on the sides and the infamous denim and leather zip that goes all across the body. I believe Grace Jones walked. Even with the McQueen that she just wore, in a way it’s that sort of vibe—the bomber jacket but with the little skirt. It’s that kind of energy: A strong, powerful woman.”.

    “There has been quite a bit of leather. The McQueen that she just wore, the Khaite full leather suit that she wore to the Vanity Fair Oscars party. She put it on, and it was like ‘This is fab.’ We were wondering if it was right for Vanity Fair and whether she would be the only one in a suit. I told Louisa that Zendaya had worn a suit the year before and I also was kind of like, ‘Fuck it, you look hot, this is great.’ Then there were two more leather Louis Vuitton looks that she wore. One was to the Vanity Fair Oscars party in 2024. And then before that, she wore a Vuitton look to the SAG Awards and the whole bodice was sculpted in leather, as well.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “Hedi Slimane is a significant inspiration of mine. Again, it’s a lot of tailoring, it’s leather, it’s a great silhouette. It’s the aesthetic overall, but in particular, it was the fall/winter 2006 collection that he did. There were things that were skinny and then there were things that were a bit more loose in terms of the trousers. There was a softness to the hardness of it all. It was still very edgy and a bit rock ‘n’ roll, but there was a soft glamour to it. That is something that I like with Louisa, even when it comes to the jewelry.”.

    Sources indicate that “I am really curious to see what Pieter Mulier will do with Versace and Atelier Versace is in January. [I should also say that] I am obsessed with Donatella Versace. When I started looking at all things [high] fashion, Donatella was another designer that I loved. That glamour and excess and sexiness—she is unapologetically who she is.”.

    “With music and ‘90s hip-hop, you look at the bling, the diamonds, and things like that. I love a great jewelry moment, so accessorizing Louisa’s looks with the right jewelry is always important part to me. I love diamonds. When she recently went to a Tiffany & Co. event [in Ashlyn], we initially had our brooch up on the lapel where you would traditionally see it. Then she was like, ‘It doesn’t feel right.’ So I moved it down to the peplum of the jacket. It was a big, big yellow diamond, which I was obsessed with. I just loved how much it sparkled and shined.”.

    “Helmut Lang is also a big inspiration. There is a Spring 1998 men's collection and a Spring 1999 collection that I think about a lot in terms of silhouette and things that still resonate today. It all comes from having researched some of those collections in the past, so they tend to be recurring elements in the work.”.

    It has been revealed that but if William’s strategy goes ahead, it wouldn’t be the first time that members of the royal family went without their HRH titles. Both Princess Anne and Prince Edward opted out of giving their children royal titles, and the former Prince Andrew was shockingly stripped of his just last year.

    Previously speaking about the decision to not bestow her children with a fancy title, Prince Edward’s wife, Sophie Wessex, told The Sunday Times, “We try to bring them up with the understanding they are very likely to have to work for a living.”.

    The Duchess of Edinburgh went on, “Hence, we made the decision not to use HRH titles.”.

    Trinity Rodman and Ben Shelton’s Complete Relationship Timeline

    📅 18 Aug 2025 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1826 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that being a professional athlete takes an inordinate amount of hard work and dedication, which is why Trinity Rodman’s romance with Ben Shelton makes so much sense.
    • In a recent development, in November 2026, multiple outlets, including People, reported that the pair had broken up.
    • In a recent development, rodman is prolific on TikTok, with more than 305,000 followers as of August 2025.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that being a professional athlete takes an inordinate amount of hard work and dedication, which is why Trinity Rodman’s romance with Ben Shelton makes so much sense. While Rodman is a soccer star, playing for the Washington Spirit and the United States women’s national soccer team, Shelton is a professional tennis champ, representing the U.S. at tournaments across the globe, including Wimbledon. Since making their relationship public in spring 2025, interest in Shelton and Rodman’s connection has only intensified.

    In a recent development, in November 2026, multiple outlets, including People, reported that the pair had broken up. Here’s what you need to know about Rodman and Shelton’s relationship timeline.

    In a recent development, rodman is prolific on TikTok, with more than 305,000 followers as of August 2025. As a result, it makes perfect sense that the star athlete appeared to tease her fresh romance with Shelton on the platform. The pair hinted that they were both “shooting their shot” with one another in a TikTok trend in March 2025, via espnW’s Instagram account. And it wasn’t long before the two athletes decided to hard-launch their romance on social media.

    On March 18, Shelton shared a series of photos on Instagram, the last of which was a mirror selfie taken with Rodman in an elevator. “I been focused, but I’m steady climbin’, I’m nowhere near my peak,” he captioned the post. The soccer player commented on her boyfriend’s post, writing, “Shooters shoot I guess,” suggesting that the TikTok most certainly paid off, as reported by The Mirror US.

    Recent findings suggest that after Shelton and Rodman revealed their relationship on Instagram, tennis pro Frances Tiafoe suggested he was actually responsible for introducing the pair. During an appearance on the TikTok account Overtime Tennis on March 18, 2025, Tiafoe said, “By the way, I don’t think people realize, I was like, the one who [connected them]—if we’re going to be real.”.

    “I’m happy for him, man,” Tiafoe said of Shelton. “The elevator photo out the gate...everybody knows who Trinity Rodman is. [The photo] at the end of the carousel, sick.”.

    However, Shelton and Rodman later denied Tiafoe’s version of events, suggesting he wasn’t responsible for them meeting. “I don’t know if I want everyone to know the story [of how we met], but I can assure you Frances was not the reason we met or got together. I don’t know why he’s taking credit for that,” Rodman told ESPN’s SportsCenter. “Me and Ben can both cut that out. It was solely a me and Ben thing.”.

    Shelton also shot down Tiafoe’s claims, telling the New York Post, “We’d like talked about her once, twice before and I was like, ‘But come on, man. You didn’t do anything.’ Putting us together, like that’s a bit of a stretch.” He continued, “[Rodman] was kind of annoyed by that. She was like, ‘Come on, bro.’ I think she noted something to him a couple times. But we’re all friends.”.

    In a recent development, after Shelton took their relationship public with his March 18, 2025 Instagram post, Rodman returned the favor by posting an adorable photo on social media, too. The picture highlighted Rodman gazing up at her tennis pro boyfriend, whose face was hidden by a baseball cap. Tagging Shelton in the photo, Rodman captioned her March 27 Instagram post, “Dibs.” Shelton commented on the post, writing, “Whoever that is he won [for sure].”.

    Sources indicate that from that point on, the romance between the two athletes seems to have only grown stronger. For instance, in an Instagram carousel posted on April 5, 2025, Shelton shared a short clip as he walked alongside Rodman, captioning the post, “In n out of time zones,” suggesting they were traveling together.

    The public’s excitement about the romance wasn’t lost on Rodman and Shelton. During an appearance on ESPN’s SportsCenter in March 2025, Rodman spoke about her decision to go public with the relationship, saying, “I mean, I’m just another person in a relationship and people know about it.” She continued, “I’m obviously very happy.”.

    In his April 2025 interview with the Latest York Post, Shelton discussed his romance with Rodman, and the incredible response they had received after revealing their relationship on Instagram. “It’s been great, obviously,” the 22-year-old athlete said. “I guess I didn’t think it would blow up as much as it did. That’s not why I did it.”.

    Sources indicate that the tennis pro also suggested that “posting your girlfriend on Instagram is a more normal thing,” so he didn’t necessarily think the photos would make such an impact. “I realized, ‘Wow, people care about my life that much,’” he told the outlet. “But yeah, [we’re] happy for sure.”.

    The same month, Rodman shared a TikTok video of herself hugging her boyfriend, with the caption, “My safety blanket...you make everyday better.”.

    In April 2025, celebrated Olympian Rodman traveled to Munich in support of Shelton, who made it all the way to the men’s singles final in the BMW Open 2025. Rodman made her debut in the player’s box when Shelton beat Francisco Cerundolo in the men’s singles semifinal, and was spotted talking to her boyfriend’s dad, Bryan Shelton, during the competition. “She’s a good luck charm,” @tennischannel wrote on Instagram. Although Shelton ultimately lost the final to Germany’s Alexander Zverev, Rodman’s presence at the tournament made their relationship status quite clear.

    In a recent development, in July 2025, Shelton made it to the quarterfinals at Wimbledon, where he ultimately lost to Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner. Rodman supported her boyfriend at the tournament in London, and she also criticized commentators for calling her the wrong name and mentioning her estranged dad, former NBA player Dennis Rodman.

    Recent findings suggest that “For those who don’t know...my name is TRINITY not Tiffany,” Rodman wrote on her Instagram Stories, via Sports Illustrated. “Also, for Ben’s matches he has his family there as his support system, which includes his dad... my dads not even in MY life no need to bring him up during HIS matches when I don’t even want him talked about during mine.”.

    According to recent reports, as well as competing across Europe throughout the summer, Shelton still found time to savor some vacation days with his girlfriend. On May 20, Shelton shared two sweet photos on Instagram, which he captioned, “Happy birthday beautiful girl...I love you.” The Olympic gold medalist responded in the comments, writing, “I luhhh you.”.

    The following month, Rodman shared footage showing her holding hands with her boyfriend as they walked around Europe. “No one else,” she captioned the Instagram post. On July 5, the Washington Spirit player shared another cute photo with Shelton, with the caption, “Watching you with googly eyes,” to which he responded, “Why am I cheesin so big.”.

    As both Shelton and Rodman are accustomed to traveling the world for their careers, they’ve had to adjust to dating while being in completely different places. “It has its challenges, but it’s definitely worth it,” Shelton told Town & Country. “It’s not something that we’re not used to—it’s been the story of our lives, especially me being on the road all the time. It’s just normal life stuff.”.

    Industry observers note that in August 2025, Rodman made her long-awaited return to soccer after taking time off to deal with a back injury. Prior to returning to work, Rodman shared vacation snaps with Shelton, along with training videos, writing on Instagram, “Not the summer that I had in mind but still loved every moment...can’t wait to be back on the field.”.

    On August 3, Rodman’s team, the Washington Spirit, played against the Portland Thorns in the National Women’s Soccer League. After joining the game for the final 14 minutes, Rodman was able to score the winning goal, cementing her triumphant return to the sport.

    Shelton wasn’t able to support his girlfriend in person, as he was in Toronto for the 2025 National Bank Open. However, he celebrated her win from afar, telling ATP Tour, “One year anniversary from her incredible goal at the Olympics, hadn’t played in 100-something days and she goes in and in 15 minutes scores a banger. It’s pretty cool, especially [because] she was emotional. I’m always happy for her.”.

    On June 14, Rodman shared a selfie with Shelton on Instagram, writing simply, “#1 fan I love you ❤️.”.

    Recent findings suggest that rodman traveled to Montreal to surprise Shelton during the Canadian Open after playing with the Washington Spirit in Washington, D.C., on August 8. She documented his reaction on her Instagram Stories, writing, “Surprised his ass, happy matchday in Montreal 😘❤️ @benshelton.”.

    Sources indicate that shelton went on to win the tournament, and Rodman celebrated his victory in an August 14 Instagram post. Alongside a photo of the couple walking together on the tennis court, she wrote, “Drive, dedication, and commitment. Back to back Canada champ! Celebrate every win baby ❤️ I love you.”.

    During an August 2026 appearance on Kylie Kelce’s Not Gonna Lie podcast, Rodman opened up about how her relationship with Shelton began, revealing that she was the one who initially reached out.

    “Everything I do is just embarrassing. I’m really embarrassed,” she stated.

    Rodman explained just how rapidly she wanted to get to know Shelton: “I fully committed to this guy that I didn’t even meet yet, for him to stay at my house for the weekend. It’s actually crazy, it’s insane, but it worked out.”.

    She also discussed why she personally embraces being called a WAG despite being a professional athlete herself.

    According to recent reports, “For me, I think I like the term personally because, like I said before, I feel like 24/7 I’m on in front of cameras…and so I think I use the term WAG for me to simplify what I’m doing,” she said. “For me, saying WAG, it’s me being like, ‘I’m Ben’s girlfriend.’ But I can understand why [the term] is so hated.”.

    Rodman added that having a partner who understands the demands of professional sports has been particularly meaningful to her.

    According to recent reports, “It’s the best feeling in the world, honestly. I think to know we’re both on the grind, running our bodies to the ground, always exhausted, doing what we love, and then to also be able to be a little like a WAG in a sense, it feels so good for us,” she said.

    Industry observers note that rodman indicated her support for Shelton after he beat Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinal of the US Open. The competitive match ended at 3:30 A.M. “My 🌎,” she wrote on her Instagram Story.

    She was also in the stands cheering him on:.

    Sources indicate that on November 24, People reported that the couple had broken up. Days before, Shelton responded “no” when asked if he would attend Rodman and the Washington Spirit’s championship game against the Kansas City Current on November 21.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read

    • It has been revealed that in fact, chrome powder paired with regular polish is so finicky that some experts feel like it’s not worth the hassle to even try.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

    There are, in my view, four types of DIY nail art: Manicures that are as easy to do as they look, designs looks complicated but are actually pretty simple, motifs that are exactly as hard as they look, and nail art that seems like it should be a breeze but are actually a pain in the butt. Chrome manicures fall into that last category, especially if you’re trying to layer the metallic powder over regular polish.

    It has been revealed that in fact, chrome powder paired with regular polish is so finicky that some experts feel like it’s not worth the hassle to even try. “In my experience, improvising with loose chrome pigment over regular polish can become a long, tedious process with inconsistent results,” notes nail artist Max Estrada. “A manicure should be a little luxury, not an endurance examination.”.

    Industry observers note that it’s a fair warning: Chrome definitely works best with gel, and it’s going to take a lot of trial and error to get that mirror-like shine on top of regular polish. But there are lots of legit reasons that some people avoid gel in their at-home manicure station (allergies... you have to buy a whole UV setup... it’s tedious to remove...), and those people might still want to try the chocolate chrome look so beloved by Hailey Bieber right now. (Also, some of us are just artistic masochists who find it reasonable that the cost of creative satisfaction would be some failed attempts and frustrated tears.).

    So, if you’re feeling up for the challenge—and have a lot of time to wait for your polish to dry completely—here are some tips for getting a chrome manicure with regular polish. (Results absolutely not guaranteed!).

    It has been revealed that while you can use any regular polish you’d like as your base color for this, there are a few different techniques that can work for a chrome finish, says Jackie of @jackie.shades. However, she’s gotten so good at applying chrome over regular polish people on the internet are calling her approach “The Jackie Method,” so I’m going to stick with that. For that method, you’ll need:.

    Chrome is not very forgiving of lumps and bumps, so you’ll need to do some careful nail prep before you get started. In addition to the usual filing, hangnail trimming, and cuticle pushing, Jackie recommends a smoothing base coat like Halo Taco Smoothing Base or What’s Up Nails Hideaway Ridge to give you a smooth base to start on.

    Industry observers note that as far as your station goes, Jackie emphasizes that chrome is messy. “Make sure you turn off any fans, work on a silicone mat or paper towel, try not to flick any dust into the air, and wear a face mask,” she says. That last point is because chrome powder is a super fine dust—you don’t want to breathe that in.

    Sources indicate that this is the method Jackie has found works best for her nails (and others on Instagram who’ve tried it say it works great for them too) but she leads with a big disclaimer that everyone is different. “Some products work for some and not for others,” Jackie states. “If something doesn’t work out, just keep experimenting.”.

    Sources indicate that after your nails are prepped, apply thin layers of your color polish of choice. Keeping them thin is important, Jackie claims, since this prevents air bubbles that will be noticeable once you add the chrome powder. Also, thin layers dry more rapidly.

    According to recent reports, having completely dry polish is one of the biggest keys to success for this look. “The base polish should be dry enough that if you press on your nail plate with your finger, it doesn’t leave any dents,” Jackie claims. In my experience, this can take hours with some polish (I told you this wasn’t some easy breezy DIY mani). If you want to be really safe, you could even paint the base color on the night and finish the next steps the following day.

    Recent findings suggest that next, you’ll be creating the tacky base for the chrome to stick to. While you can use any quick dry top coat here, Jackie recommends a 3-free (meaning it’s free of toluene, formaldehyde, and dibutyl phthalate) formula for ease. “ Toluene can sometimes cause certain nail polish colors to ‘bleed’ or ‘run’ so this just helps to avoid any unnecessary cleanup,” she says.

    Sources indicate that again, you’ll need to let this layer dry until you don’t get any dents if you press into it. Luckily, this usually takes less than five minutes with a quick dry. “I cannot emphasize enough the importance of letting each layer dry,” Jackie indicates. “Most problems that come up (polish wrinkling, bubbles, weird texture, chrome looking cloudy etc.) are because one of the layers wasn't fully dry.”.

    Finally, the fun part. Jackie uses her finger to apply the chrome (but only on regular polish—doing so on gel could lead to skin irritation) but you can also use an eyeshadow sponge or cosmetic wedge.

    It has been revealed that to apply, tap your tool of choice into the chrome powder pot and gently wipe it onto the nail. Then, use the tool to buff the chrome into your nail until it creates a smooth, metallic finish. Once you’re happy with how it looks, use a big fluffy brush to brush away the excess.

    Once the chrome is applied, wait at least another 15 minutes to ensure the top coat underneath it is truly, 100% dry. Then, Jackie indicates to swipe a 240 grit buffer block along the free edge of your nail to remove any excess chrome powder. “Now, brush off any additional excess and use a clean cosmetic wedge to gently wipe and tap over the nail to get any leftover loose chrome,” she says.

    After lots of trial and error, Jackie found that the alcohol-based top coat DRK Seal Glaze “keeps the mirror shine and stays on nails longer than a water-based top coat.” You’ll want to apply two coats of it at this point, waiting about 10 minutes (or until the cloudiness turns clear) in between each coat. Make sure you’re applying thin coats that go all the way to the edges of your nails—if you miss any spots, those areas could turn glittery. Then, wait at least 30 minutes for the glaze to dry completely.

    After everything is completely dry, you’ll want to finish with the same top coat you applied before the chrome powder. Even on gel polish chrome is notoriously prone to chipping, but Jackie notes this glaze + top coat combo helps with longevity, especially if you use the top coat to wrap the tip of your nail.

    Unlike with gels, removal is way easier than applying here: Jackie notes you can take this off just like you would any other regular polish manicure.

    If all of this is making your head spin, Estrada notes that there are some chrome-effect regular polishes that can get pretty close to this mirror-like finish. “A chrome-effect lacquer is an alternative finish, not a promise that every bottle will reproduce the same mirror effect as a professional pigment-and-gel system,” he says. “The key thing is to choose the right product for the finish you want, rather than expect an improvised combination to perform identically.” Sally Hansen and Essie, both sell chrome-effect polishes, though they do look more glittery than a true chrome finish. There’s no shame in this game, Estrada says: “There’s nothing wrong with taking the more straightforward route.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that cher Horowitz had a touch-screen conveyer belt in her color-coded closet. Carrie Bradshaw kept her Manolos in an unusually spacious high-fashion-filled walk-in. And Margot Robbie’s Barbie displayed her hot-pink wardrobe like doll’s packaging in her wall-free fantasy villa. Danielle Lauder, the great-granddaughter of Estée Lauder, created her own iteration of the dream closet—this time, in real life.

    According to recent reports, her own inspiration? “I always thought of Belle in Beauty and the Beast in the library, just rolling around on her ladder,” she claims. “I’m not much of a reader, but as a collector, I knew that’s what I wanted.”.

    According to recent reports, her wish list for the jewel-box space also included curving walls, glossy pink lacquer, illuminated marble, and a capsule-shaped vanity inspired by the makeup collection she designed for Estée Lauder in 2019. The beauty empire was founded by—and named after—her great-grandmother in 1946; and her father, William P. Lauder, serves as the chairman of the board. (Danielle now oversees her own production company, Act 4 Artists.).

    Sources indicate that to make her dream a reality, Lauder turned to architects Goil Amornvivat and Thomas Morbitzer, founders of Newly introduced York City–based AMMOR Architecture. The duo had instant chemistry with Lauder, who was especially taken with the meticulous diorama they created for her.

    “Tom and I both love Barbie,” indicates Amornvivat. “So we tweaked our design process to make an architectural model that was more like a dollhouse, where you could switch out surfaces.” Their efforts worked on Lauder, herself a Barbie fan, and the pair walked away with the commission to not just create the dressing room but to overhaul the entire industrial-style apartment in the West Village of Manhattan, which was then being used as an art studio.

    Sources indicate that “They both really understood and saw my vision,” says Lauder. “Plus, they were the most excited, which made me more excited. Goil is like the Energizer Bunny.”.

    It has been revealed that the 250-square-foot dressing room is, Lauder says, “the biggest room in the apartment besides the living room.” It’s also where Lauder spends the most time. She enters just off the primary bedroom via an arched passageway finished in custom bronze plaster, emerging from the dark portal into a pink fantasia where her expansive fashion collection is arrayed like a personal boutique. “The idea was for it to be part display area but also a functional closet,” she says.

    At the center is a custom pink vanity outfitted with fluted drawers, dual-sided mirrors, and a top made of richly veined Midnight Rose marble, sourced from New York Stone. Lauder keeps her collection of vintage and reissued Estée Lauder compacts in the drawers. “I love collecting them and having them out on display or in a nice drawer,” claims Lauder. “They’re beautiful little artifacts.”.

    Industry observers note that on the curving walls, rounded niches display shelving and racks against illuminated stone, part of Lauder’s request for layered lighting. “I love the backlit marble,” she says. “It’s so flattering.” She keeps her enviable bag and shoe collection on permanent display, maintained with help from her housekeeper. Lauder draws from the selection on a daily basis, with particular affection for family heirlooms such as her mom’s vintage Dolce & Gabbana handbags.

    Overhead, Amornvivat and Morbitzer devised a futuristic lighting installation, stretching mesh taut over an oval-shaped light source to create a seamless surface. “The light in there is controllable by color, and it's dimmable,” notes Morbitzer. “It’s kind of like a skylight, which was important because it’s the only room without windows,” adds Amornvivat.

    Recent findings suggest that the bespoke elements continue: heated floors, an ice maker, a perfume bar, plenty of drawers, and a pair of walk-in closets cleverly concealed behind matching lacquered doors. “The whole room is custom millwork,” indicates Amornvivat.

    Recent findings suggest that and Lauder did get the sliding ladder of her dreams. “That was my hill to die on,” she indicates. “I’ve always struggled to reach things in my closet, so it was definitely practical. And my grandfather had one in his apartment in the library when I was growing up, and I just loved it.”.

    Now that the closet is complete, Lauder has a hard time leaving. “I spend more time in here than I do probably even sleeping in bed,” she says with a laugh. The space is remarkably faithful to the original idea that Amornvivat and Morbitzer presented in their dollhouse diorama. “I wanted it to be totally mine, feminine and fun, and still very warm and inviting,” she says. “It’s become my ultimate bachelorette hub.”.

    Recent findings suggest that geoffrey Montes is an associate editor at ELLE Decor with a serious love for all things real estate and design. Before that, he worked at Architectural Digest, Galerie, and Preservation magazines, covering everything from jaw-dropping listings to world-famous architects and design events like Salone del Mobile and Homo Faber.

    Front Office: Radhi Devlukia
